knowledge_point.title: Finding an Integral That Represents the Surface Area of a Parametric Surface

question.:question/problem:
$$
\iint_D\boxed{}\,\mathrm{d}A,\quad D=\{(u,v):0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 2\}
$$

The integral above gives the surface area of the parametric surface $r(u,v)=\langle u + v,\,3 - v,\,2 u + 3 v + 1\rangle$ for $0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 2.$ What is the missing expression?
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
\iint_S\mathrm{d}S=\iint_D\left\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\right\|\,\mathrm{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u &=\langle \frac{\partial x}{\partial u},\,\frac{\partial y}{\partial u},\,\frac{\partial z}{\partial u}\rangle \\  &=\langle \frac{\partial}{\partial u}\left(u + v\right),\,\frac{\partial}{\partial u}\left(3 - v\right),\,\frac{\partial}{\partial u}\left(2 u + 3 v + 1\right)\rangle \\  &=\langle 1,\,0,\,2\rangle \\ \mathbf r_v &=\langle \frac{\partial x}{\partial v},\,\frac{\partial y}{\partial v},\,\frac{\partial z}{\partial v}\rangle \\  &=\langle \frac{\partial}{\partial v}\left(u + v\right),\,\frac{\partial}{\partial v}\left(3 - v\right),\,\frac{\partial}{\partial v}\left(2 u + 3 v + 1\right)\rangle \\  &=\langle 1,\,-1,\,3\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v &=\begin{vmatrix}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & 3\end{vmatrix} \\  &=\langle \begin{vmatrix}0 & 2 \\ -1 & 3\end{vmatrix},\,-\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{vmatrix},\,\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1\end{vmatrix}\rangle \\  &=\langle 2,\,-1,\,-1\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\left\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\right\| &=\left\|\langle 2,\,-1,\,-1\rangle\right\| \\  &=\sqrt{\left(2\right)^2+\left(-1\right)^2+\left(-1\right)^2} \\  &=\sqrt{4+1+1} \\  &=\sqrt{6} \\  &=\sqrt{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface area is

$$
\begin{aligned}\iint_S\mathrm{d}S &=\iint_D\left\|\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v\right\|\,\mathrm{d}A \\  &=\iint_D \sqrt{6}\,\mathrm{d}A\end{aligned}
$$
